skill.name: orca-cli
skill.description: Operate Orca-managed worktrees, folder contexts, terminals, repos, automations, artifacts, skill sharing, worktree comments, and Orca's embedded browser through the `orca` CLI. Use when the user says "$orca-cli", "Orca worktree", "child worktree", "spawn codex/claude in a worktree", "read/wait/send Orca terminal", "handoff" / "handover" / "give this to another agent", "Orca browser", "orca artifacts", or "share skills". Prefer it over raw git worktree, ad hoc PTYs, or Computer Use when Orca state is involved. Use Computer Use only when a visible window needs GUI control that a CLI, filesystem, or API cannot do.
skill.summary: Select the session-specific Orca executable and load its matching CLI guide for workspace operations.
skill.author: agc2020

security_audit.summary: All 18 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting and references to shell names. A separate semantic concern is unconditional permission escalation after sandbox denial. No evidence found of credential theft, exfiltration, or audit manipulation in the reviewed stub; the runtime-loaded guide was unavailable for review.

remediation.issue: The recovery instructions request escalated permissions after sandbox denial without explicitly requiring authorization.
remediation.suggestion: Require applicable policy checks and explicit approval before escalation; otherwise report the denial and stop.

content.user_title: Load Orca CLI Guidance for Your Workspace
content.value_statement: Using the wrong Orca executable can target another build or launch an unrelated program. This skill selects the session executable and retrieves its version-matched guide.
actual_capabilities: Provides executable-selection rules for managed sessions, development checkouts, and Linux terminals.
Documents retrieving the version-matched orca-cli guide from the selected executable.
Warns against accidentally launching the GNOME Orca screen reader on Linux.
Directs agents to reuse one executable and stop if it cannot run.
Recommends JSON output and CLI help for discovering supported commands.
Provides startup and outdated-command recovery guidance.
limitations: Requires an available Orca executable; the skill does not install Orca.
Detailed workspace operations depend on a runtime-loaded guide that is not included in this package.
The stub does not document specific worktree, browser, artifact, or terminal operation flags.
Sandbox access may require explicit approval; this skill cannot authorize permission escalation.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Development Session
use_cases.description: Select the correct Orca executable and load its guide before managing worktrees.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Agent Handoff
use_cases.description: Retrieve current CLI guidance before coordinating another agent through Orca-managed terminals.

use_cases.title: Diagnose CLI Availability
use_cases.description: Identify executable errors, missing guide support, or runtime access restrictions without guessing unsupported commands.

prompt_templates.title: Find the Session Executable
prompt_templates.prompt: Determine the Orca executable for this session using the skill rules. Explain your selection without changing workspace state.

prompt_templates.title: Load Current Guidance
prompt_templates.prompt: Resolve the Orca executable and retrieve its orca-cli guide. Summarize available operations without executing workspace changes.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Guide Error
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate why the Orca guide cannot load. Report the exact error and use read-only help where supported. Do not escalate without approval.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Worktree Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Load the matching Orca guide and plan a child-worktree handoff to another agent. Confirm supported commands and request approval before state changes.

output_examples.input: Which executable should I use on Linux outside an Orca-managed terminal?
output_examples.output: Use orca-ide unless a higher-priority session rule applies. Bare orca may launch the GNOME screen reader.

output_examples.input: The selected executable cannot run. Should I try another Orca build?
output_examples.output: Report the exact error and stop. Switching executables may target a different Orca build.

output_examples.input: The guide command is unknown in my Orca installation.
output_examples.output: Update Orca to restore guide retrieval. Until then, use CLI help for read-only discovery and do not guess unsupported commands.

best_practices: Resolve the executable once and reuse it throughout the session.
Load the matching guide before workspace operations and prefer JSON output.
Respect sandbox restrictions and obtain required approval before requesting additional access.
anti_patterns: Running bare orca on Linux outside a managed terminal without checking executable-selection rules.
Switching to a different Orca executable after the selected one fails.
Guessing unsupported commands or treating sandbox denial as automatic permission to escalate.

faq.question: What does this skill include?
faq.answer: It includes executable-selection and guide-loading instructions. Detailed operation guidance comes from the selected Orca executable.

faq.question: Does this skill install Orca?
faq.answer: No. An available Orca executable is required.

faq.question: Which AI tools are listed as supported?
faq.answer: The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Why should I avoid bare orca on Linux?
faq.answer: Outside Orca-managed terminals, it may resolve to the GNOME screen reader. The skill selects orca-ide unless a higher-priority rule applies.

faq.question: What happens if guide retrieval is unsupported?
faq.answer: The stub recommends updating Orca and using help for read-only discovery. It prohibits guessing unsupported commands.

faq.question: Does sandbox denial permit automatic escalation?
faq.answer: No. Follow host policy and obtain required approval. If escalation is unavailable or denied, report the restriction and stop.
